doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Why the blues grabs people
summary: He sees the blues as the first form and the music of black culture.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Is it possible to put into words what is so attractive — I don’t know if that’s the right word — but the blues just seems to grab people. Have you ever been able to understand why that is?

Not really. I guess it was one of the — it was the first form. Blues, and then jazz. It was definitely one of the more common harmonic structures for jazz tunes. It goes all the way back to the St. Louis Blues, Bessie Smith, and it was definitely a production of the black culture here in the United States, it’s the blues. And jazz I guess — the main players of this music were black people, and it’s just like the blues is like the music of our people. It’s infectious, everybody likes the blues, but nobody wants to have them.
